_comment: script_beats is the spine — the narration broken into beats, reconstructed from the takes (transcribe.py gets you close enough). Every asset then hangs off a beat id. Keep gists in plain language: they are what a future session reads first.

script_beats.gist: Hook. A compilation of me practicing — and there's an obnoxious buzzing in the background. That sound is called the drone. Why would I voluntarily inflict this? Let me explain.

The exception. For a specific set of intervals the overtone frequency is an integer multiple of the pure frequency, so overtones reinforce instead of colliding. The PERFECT INTERVALS — fifth 3:2, fourth 4:3, octave 2:1.

_comment_assets: role = short title; prefix ★ when the video would be materially worse without it. shows = what is literally on screen (or, for text, what it says). use = where it earns its place, tied to a beat and ideally a spoken line. beat = a script beat id, or 'any' (flexible), 'reference' (not source footage), 'patch' (retake fragment), 'unused' (no home found). k = video | image | audio | text.
_comment_binding: binds_to and tags are what make /real-storyboarding able to attach this file to a mock component in the notebook. binds_to = the kind of component this asset could satisfy, written in the creator's own notebook vocabulary (quote the angle-bracket shape). tags = short lowercase slugs, so a notebook component carrying '#drone-demo' finds this file. Both are optional and the catalogue still works without them — it just binds worse.

assets.shows: Narration, 24.8s. Opens on the practice compilation and names the buzzing as the drone; sets up the 'why inflict this' question.
assets.use: B1. The authoritative clock for the opening. Pairs with practice b-roll + suffering memes.
assets.binds_to: the narration spine for the hook — a `<Have you ever heard…>` type component, i.e. the spoken line itself

assets.shows: Three stacked panels: a slow wave, a fast wave, and their sum.
assets.use: The single most important diagram in the folder. It is the literal picture of the whole argument. B3 into B4.
assets.binds_to: a `<show image of two waves adding up / interfering>` type component

assets.shows: Dark panel, two labelled sine waves (2f and 3f), caption '3:2 the PERFECT FIFTH'. One of a matched set of three.
assets.use: B5. Second in the set — reveal the three in sequence as the ratios are named. NOTE: the real filename contains U+202F before 'PM'; the builder resolves this.
assets.binds_to: a `<show the ratio panel for the perfect fifth>` type component; the matched set covers three consecutive such components

assets.shows: 15.6s, 2192x2928 @120fps. POV over the violin: bow, strings, left hand, office background. Short and purpose-shot.
assets.use: The dissonant demo — audible beating. Verify by ear before locking. Pairs with B4.
assets.binds_to: a `<video clip of me playing the two notes on one string>` type component — the beating demo

assets.shows: 84 lines / 610 words of Markdown. Section headers HOOK / PROBLEM / THE MATH / DEMO / PAYOFF, with the perfect-interval ratios spelled out and two alternate hook lines at the top.
assets.use: Ground truth for the wording of every beat — the takes drift from it, so where a transcript and this file disagree, the recording wins and this explains what was intended. Read it before reconstructing script_beats.
